response.sql: WITH type_counts AS (SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderspivot) AS cnt FROM riskandmargin rm JOIN orders o ON rm.ordervault = o.recordvault WHERE o.ordertune IS NOT NULL GROUP BY o.ordertune), avg_cnt AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_count FROM type_counts) SELECT AVG(tc.cnt) AS avg_count_above_average, AVG(tc.cnt - ac.avg_count) AS avg_excess_over_average FROM type_counts tc CROSS JOIN avg_cnt ac WHERE tc.cnt > ac.avg_count;

assumptions.assumption: The average across types is the unweighted mean of the per-type distinct-order counts, computed only over order types that have at least one matched risk/margin record.
Orders with a NULL ordertune are not treated as an order type and are excluded from the per-type counts.
Distinct orders are identified by orders.orderspivot, the primary key, so each order is counted once per type regardless of how many risk/margin records it has.
The inner join against orders drops risk/margin records whose ordervault has no matching recordvault, as the request specifies.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat orders with a NULL ordertune as their own order-type group and include that group in the per-type counts and the cross-type average.
